text: In November 2024, an AI agent guarding a prize pool of about forty-seven thousand dollars was talked into giving all of it away.
In March, someone broke into another agent's dashboard, and fifty-five and a half ETH walked out the door.
Researchers then showed that one planted memory could make an agent pay an attacker.
Every one of these agents could move the money itself.
That's why Sovra exists. Your agent can pay, but you keep the final say.
Here's the same trick, live on NEAR testnet. The invoice hides an instruction. The model refuses, and when we force it through anyway, the vault rejects it on-chain.
Swap the recipient after the decision is signed, and the signature no longer matches. Refused. Nothing moves.
And if the controls are compromised, the agent's key can still only ask. One signature from the owner's wallet freezes everything.
On a normal day, routine invoices just get paid, and the agent earns trust each time NEAR confirms one.
Anything unusual waits in the vault, with a countdown, until you approve it from your own wallet.
The vault was attacked nine different ways. Every attempt was refused, and not a single NEAR moved.
Give your agent a budget. Not a blank cheque.
Sovra. Live now on NEAR testnet.
